subject: Medivance: request for temporary logging carveout and evidence flow
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@medivance.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Jake Torres <jake.torres@medivance.com>, security@medivance.com
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary log retention carveout: request and evidence ask

Hi Stephanie,

Following our SOC 2 readiness review, our security team has asked for a temporary carveout to retain a narrow set of application request logs for 90 days (instead of your standard 30d) for a scheduled clinical-data ingestion run the week of 2027-04-12. The requirement is scoped to the Medivance tenant only and limited to ingest/forensics metadata (request timestamp, request-id, model id, routing decision, and anonymized user-hash) — not raw customer PII or content.

We need two things to progress: 1) a brief design note describing how Redwood will isolate/segregate the retained logs and control access; and 2) an evidence package we can attach to our audit showing the retention exception was implemented (log filter rules, preserved audit trail, and proof-of-delete after the 90d window).

I've attached our SIG questions extract and a CSV with the specific event types we want retained. Can Redwood confirm feasibility and a proposed timeline?

Thanks,
Alice Monroe
Sr. Security Ops, Medivance
-- attachment: medivance_sig_questions_v4.pdf (pdf) --
-- attachment: log-sampling-matrix.csv (csv) --

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@medivance.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary log retention carveout: request and evidence ask

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear scope and the matrix. We can support a tenant-scoped extension for specific event types, but there are a few operational controls we need to confirm before sign-off:

- Implementation approach: create a tenant-scoped filtered bucket (immutable for the retention window) that receives only the event types you listed; no model response content will be included.
- Access controls: RBAC role for "Medivance-forensics" with timeboxed access; only a named Red- and Medivance security admin can unlock.
- Evidence: we can provide the following artifacts at the end of the 90d window — a) policy/implementation note, b) log filter rule JSON (redacted), c) access audit trail (who retrieved the data), d) proof-of-delete workflow runbook + signed deletion receipt.

To scope effort and timeline we need: a) confirmation of the exact event types (looks like you included 12 rows in the CSV), b) the start and end dates for the 90d window, and c) whether Medivance needs the preserved logs in-place or exported to a Medivance-controlled S3.

I'll loop in engineering to draft the design note and the evidence template. Proposed next step: a short 30-min sync tomorrow to agree on export vs in-place retention.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Temporary log retention carveout: implementation options + evidence checklist

Stephanie — draft notes for the design and evidence package below (we'll turn into the formal doc once Alice confirms the CSV rows):

1) Implementation options (pros/cons)
  - In-place tenant-scoped retention (fastest): filter writes into a tenant-scoped archive namespace with object immutability flag set for 91 days. Pros: minimal data movement. Cons: requires additional storage tagging and small runtime routing change.
  - Export to Medivance S3 (strong separation): stream matching events to a Medivance-controlled bucket. Pros: clear separation and easier customer evidence chain. Cons: requires secure cross-account write and additional encryption envelope handling.

2) Controls we will provide
  - Filter rule definition (hash of rule + human readable)
  - Immutable object storage for 91 days and automated deletion job with signed receipt
  - Access gating via timebound RBAC and MFA unlock by two administrators
  - Audit trail of any reads (+ minimal retained headers)

3) Evidence deliverables
  - Implementation note (design diagram + config snippets)
  - Redacted filter rule file (we will include rule hash and description)
  - Audit log export showing admin access events (timebound)
  - Signed deletion receipt and deletion job logs after 91 days
  - Optional: proof-of-export (if sending to customer S3) — STS token creation + put-object logs

4) Timeline estimate
  - Confirm CSV rows & window: +1 day after Alice confirmation
  - Engineering change + staging validation: 3 business days
  - Coordination with Medivance and dry-run: 2 business days
  - Total (from confirmation): ~6 business days

I'm happy to own the implementation ticket and produce the evidence pack. Thoughts on export vs in-place?

-- Priyom
Sr. Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@medivance.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Jake Torres <jake.torres@medivance.com>, security@medivance.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary log retention carveout: request and evidence ask

Thanks — preference is export to our S3 (separation is important for our auditors). Start date 2027-04-12 and end date 2027-07-10 (90 days inclusive). The CSV is final (we've redacted any identifiers). Two clarifications: 1) will the exported objects contain any request payload or only metadata fields listed in the CSV? 2) we need an interim proof-of-setup snapshot (a signed export manifest after the first week) so we can show auditors we've configured the carveout prior to the ingest run.

If export requires cross-account write, we'll provide a 1-week window to provision the S3 role.

Alice

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@medivance.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 12:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary log retention carveout: final plan + next steps

Hi Alice — thanks for confirming the window and export preference. We prefer export to Medivance S3 as well for a clean evidence chain. A few operational notes and next steps: 

- We will stream only the metadata fields listed (no payloads). The export will be encrypted server-side with a customer-provided KMS envelope if you prefer.
- To reduce blast radius, we will create a dedicated IAM principal with PutObject-only rights for the target bucket; Redwood will not store long-term copies beyond the 90d retention on your side.
- Evidence timeline: a) setup manifest (signed) within 3 business days of role provisioning; b) weekly export manifest during the retention window (automated); c) signed deletion receipt when the 91-day deletion job runs.

Action items:
1) Medivance to provision a cross-account role (we'll send the ARN + trust policy).
2) Medivance to confirm KMS requirement (yes/no).
3) Redwood (Priyom) to create SEC-742 ticket and a draft implementation note.

I'll add the SEC-742 ticket and the draft doc to the HubSpot record. Once we have the role ARN we can schedule the dry-run.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
-- attachment: log-sampling-matrix.csv (csv) --

From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@medivance.com>

Cc: Jake Torres <jake.torres@medivance.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary log retention carveout: final plan + next steps

Thanks Rishi — we'll provision the role today and confirm KMS by EOD. Appreciate the clear deliverables; the auditors asked us to capture the signed setup manifest after the first weekly export, so please include the manifest format in SEC-742.

I'll expect the ARN and the dry-run window once the ticket is created.

Regards,
Alice Monroe
Sr. Security Ops, Medivance
